claim: The Legislature convenes at noon on the first Monday in February each year and must adjourn sine die by 5 p.m. on the last Friday in May
quote: The Legislature shall meet in regular session at the seat of government at twelve o'clock noon on the first Monday in February of each year and the regular session shall be finally adjourned sine die not later than five o'clock p.m. on the last Friday in May of each year.

claim: In odd-numbered years the Legislature also meets for one organizational day on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in January
quote: on the first Tuesday after the first Monday in January of each odd numbered year

claim: During the session the governor has five days, Sundays excepted, to act on a bill or it becomes law without signature
quote: If any bill or resolution shall not be returned by the Governor within five days (Sundays excepted) after it shall have been presented to him, the same shall be a law in like manner as if he had signed it

claim: After final adjournment a bill becomes law only if the governor approves it within 15 days
quote: No bill shall become a law after the final adjournment of the Legislature, unless approved by the Governor within fifteen days after such adjournment.

claim: An act takes effect 90 days after the session adjourns unless two-thirds of each house votes an emergency clause
quote: No act shall take effect until ninety days after the adjournment of the session at which it was passed

claim: An emergency clause needs two-thirds of all members elected to each house
quote: the Legislature, by a vote of two-thirds of all members elected to each House, so directs

claim: Every election run by a county election board is held on a Tuesday
quote: No election required to be conducted by any county election board shall be scheduled for a day other than Tuesday.

claim: Counties, school districts, municipalities, fire protection districts and other subdivisions may hold regular or special elections only on the dates listed in § 3-101(B)
quote: no regular or special election for any purpose shall be held by any county, school district, technology center school district, municipality, fire protection district, or other political subdivision authorized to call elections except as follows

claim: The allowed local dates include the second Tuesday of February, first Tuesday of April, third Tuesday of June, fourth Tuesday of August and the November general election date in any year
quote: 1. The second Tuesday of February in any year; 2. The first Tuesday of April in any year; 3. The third Tuesday of June in any year; 4. The fourth Tuesday of August in any year;

claim: A December date is also allowed, but only every fourth year starting December 2025 (2025 amendment)
quote: The second Tuesday of December, beginning in December of 2025, and every four (4) years thereafter.

claim: Municipal elections, including those of home rule charter cities, may be held only on the § 3-101 dates
quote: All municipal elections, including elections for municipalities with home rule charters, shall be held only on dates identified in Section 3-101 of this title.

claim: The general election is the first Tuesday after the first Monday in November of even-numbered years, and county officers whose terms are ending are elected then
quote: state, district and county officers, whose terms expire before the next succeeding General Election, shall be elected

claim: The party primary is the third Tuesday in June of each even-numbered year
quote: A Primary Election shall be held on the third Tuesday in June of each even-numbered year

claim: A party nominee needs a majority in the primary; otherwise the top two meet in a runoff primary on the fourth Tuesday of August
quote: receives a majority of all votes cast for all candidates of such party for the office

claim: Runoff primary date
quote: Runoff Primary Election to be held on the fourth Tuesday of August in the same year

claim: Primaries are closed: a voter may vote only in the primary of the party they are registered with
quote: except the political party of which his registration form shows him to be a member

claim: A recognized party may choose to let voters registered as Independents vote in its primary
quote: A recognized political party may permit registered voters designated as Independents

claim: An Independent voter may vote in only one party's primary
quote: A registered voter designated as Independent shall not be permitted to vote in a Primary Election or Runoff Primary Election of more than one party.

claim: A party's decision to admit Independents is made every odd-numbered November and covers the next two calendar years
quote: between November 1 and 30 of every odd-numbered year

claim: An unopposed candidate is deemed nominated or elected and does not appear on the ballot
quote: Any candidate who is unopposed in any election shall be deemed to have been nominated or elected

claim: A party candidate for county office must have been registered with that party for six months before filing
quote: must have been a registered voter of that party for the six-month period

claim: An independent candidate for county office must have been registered as an Independent for six months before filing
quote: To file as an independent candidate for any state or county office, a person must have been registered to vote as an independent for the six-month period

claim: County and state candidates file with either a filing fee or a supporting petition
quote: A declaration of candidacy must be accompanied by

claim: The petition alternative is a share of registered voters in the district or county (no signature counts in copy)
quote: A petition supporting a candidate's filing signed by not fewer than two percent

claim: Independent and other non-party candidates appear on the November general election ballot after the party nominees
quote: followed by independent candidates in lot

claim: County nominees are party nominees certified after the primary and runoff
quote: The county election board shall certify a list of nominees of each political party for county offices

claim: District judges and associate district judges are elected without party designation
quote: district judges and associate district judges shall be without party designation.

claim: An associate district judge candidate who wins a majority at the June primary is elected outright
quote: the candidate who received the majority of all votes cast at the Primary Election shall be deemed to have been elected to that office

claim: Oklahoma has 77 counties
quote: seventy-seven counties of Oklahoma

claim: Each county is divided into three commissioner districts
quote: Each county shall be divided by the board of county commissioners into three (3) compact districts

claim: Each commissioner is elected by the voters of their own district
quote: One commissioner shall be elected from each of the districts by the voters of the district

claim: Commissioners from districts 1 and 3 are elected on the cycle that began in 1990 (governor's-race years), four-year terms
quote: two county commissioners, one from the first county commissioner district and one from the third county commissioner district

claim: The district 2 commissioner is elected on the cycle that began in 1996 (presidential years), four-year term
quote: one county commissioner from the second county commissioner district, who shall hold office for a term of four (4) years

claim: The court clerk, sheriff and county clerk are elected every four years on the cycle that began in 1976 (presidential years)
quote: At the general election to be held in November 1976, and each four (4) years thereafter, there shall be elected in each county of the state, a court clerk, a county sheriff, and a county clerk

claim: The county assessor and treasurer are elected every four years on the cycle that began in 1974 (governor's-race years)
quote: there shall be elected in each county of the state, a county assessor and a county treasurer

claim: Constitution created three county commissioners in each county, subject to change by the Legislature
quote: three County Commissioners

claim: Only a county under 550,000 people that contains a metro area of 250,000 or more may adopt a County Home Rule Charter
quote: Any county in this state with a population of less than five hundred fifty thousand (550,000)

claim: Home rule charter population test, second half
quote: which contains a metropolitan area with a population of two hundred fifty thousand (250,000) or more

claim: A charter county's governing body must be elected, with terms of no more than four years
quote: The term for service of the governing body shall not exceed four (4) years.

claim: A county charter may not conflict with state sovereignty and established public policy
quote: contrary to or inconsistent with the sovereignty and established public policies of this state

claim: Each county may vote to abolish township government
quote: abolish township organization or government

claim: A municipality is an incorporated city or town
quote: means any incorporated city or town

claim: A place needs at least 1,000 inhabitants to incorporate as a city
quote: which population must be one thousand (1,000) inhabitants or more

claim: A town becomes a city only if its voters approve; growth alone does not change its class
quote: the question of whether or not the town shall become a city

claim: A city or town of 2,000 or more may frame a charter
quote: Any city or town containing a population of two thousand (2,000) inhabitants or more

claim: Constitutional charter power for cities over 2,000; the charter must be approved by the governor
quote: Any city containing a population of more than two thousand inhabitants may frame a charter for its own government

claim: A charter prevails over conflicting municipal law in force when it was adopted
quote: the provisions of the charter shall prevail

claim: The statutory municipal election article does not apply to charter cities, which must still use § 3-101 dates
quote: shall not apply to any municipality which is governed by charter

claim: General municipal elections in statutory cities and towns are the first Tuesday in April of odd-numbered years
quote: General municipal elections shall be held in cities and towns on the first Tuesday in April in each odd-numbered year.

claim: In statutory cities and towns, ward seats are elected by the voters of the whole municipality
quote: including those from wards as well as at large, shall be elected at large by the registered voters of the entire municipality

claim: Municipal elections are nonpartisan, with every candidate filing as an independent, unless the municipality has a partisan-primary ordinance
quote: Municipal elections shall be nonpartisan and all candidates shall file as independent candidates unless

claim: A nonpartisan municipal election has no primary
quote: No primary elections shall be held in a nonpartisan election.

claim: A charter city may provide otherwise on partisanship by charter or ordinance
quote: any municipality which is governed by a charter may provide otherwise by charter or ordinance

claim: Any municipality may adopt an ordinance making its elections partisan
quote: A municipality may adopt an ordinance requiring its elections to be partisan.

claim: Without notice to the county election board the election defaults to nonpartisan
quote: then the municipal election shall be on a nonpartisan basis

claim: A partisan municipal primary is the second Tuesday of February in odd-numbered years
quote: A primary election shall be held in cities and towns on the second Tuesday of February in each odd-numbered year

claim: Municipal candidates pay no filing fee and file no petition
quote: shall not be required to post a filing fee, nor shall they be required to file petitions

claim: Running in a nonpartisan municipal election does not affect the candidate's party registration
quote: shall not affect one's party affiliation or regularity

claim: The default term for an elected municipal official is four years
quote: the term of office of an elected municipal official shall be four (4) years

claim: Statutory aldermanic city: mayor elected at large plus one or two councilmembers per ward
quote: shall consist of the mayor, who is elected at large, and one or two councilmembers from each ward of the city

claim: Aldermanic voters may switch between one and two councilmembers per ward
quote: The governing body may submit to the voters the question of whether one or two councilmembers shall be elected from each ward.

claim: Aldermanic cities elect a clerk, marshal, street commissioner and treasurer by default
quote: 4. The marshal; and 5. The street commissioner.

claim: Voters may make the aldermanic marshal, street commissioner, clerk or treasurer appointed
quote: of the city marshal, the street commissioner, the city clerk, the city treasurer

claim: Statutory council-manager city: one councilmember per ward plus one at large
quote: shall consist of one (1) councilmember from each ward of the city and one (1) councilmember at large

claim: In a council-manager city the council chooses the mayor
quote: The council shall elect from among its members a mayor and a vice-mayor.

claim: Statutory strong-mayor-council city: mayor elected at large and serves as at-large councilmember
quote: The mayor shall serve as ex officio councilmember at large.

claim: Statutory town: three or five trustees, nominated from wards or at large and elected at large
quote: The town board of trustees shall consist of either three (3) or five (5) trustees who shall be nominated from wards or at large and elected at large.

claim: Town voters may change the board between three and five trustees
quote: The governing body may submit to the voters the question of whether the town board shall consist of either three (3) or five (5) trustees.

claim: In a town the trustees choose the mayor from among themselves
quote: The board of trustees shall elect from among its members a mayor.

claim: Towns elect a clerk and treasurer by default, on staggered four-year terms
quote: In a statutory town, the terms of the elected officers shall be staggered

claim: Town voters may make the clerk or treasurer appointed
quote: the question of providing for the appointment by the board of trustees of the town clerk, the town treasurer

claim: At-large town trustees are elected by plurality
quote: The candidate who receives a plurality of the votes cast for the office of trustee for the designated term shall be elected

claim: Non-charter municipalities under 2,000 elect officers at a biennial town meeting unless they opt into county-run elections by ordinance
quote: at biennial town meetings or special town meetings of the voters of each municipality

claim: Town meeting act applies to non-charter municipalities with fewer than 2,000 residents
quote: all municipalities with fewer than two thousand (2,000) residents

claim: A small municipality may opt out of town meetings by ordinance
quote: may at any time adopt an ordinance requiring that its officers shall be elected

claim: The biennial town meeting is the first Tuesday in April of odd-numbered years
quote: a biennial town meeting of the voters shall be held on the first Tuesday in April in each odd-numbered year

claim: A municipality in more than one county has its elections run by the county where its central offices are
quote: Elections for a municipality which is located in more than one county shall be conducted by the county election board of the county wherein said municipality's central offices are located.

claim: School districts are independent, elementary or technology center districts
quote: shall be designated only as independent, elementary or technology center school districts

claim: Elementary districts offer kindergarten through eighth grade
quote: Elementary school districts shall offer grades kindergarten through eight

claim: School board general election is the first Tuesday of April every year
quote: The general election of members of the board of education of every school district and technology center school district shall be conducted on the first Tuesday of April of each year.

claim: School board primary, when needed, is the second Tuesday in February (moved to the presidential primary date in a year when that is in February)
quote: shall be conducted on the second Tuesday in February of each year, except in any year when a Presidential Preferential Primary is held in February

claim: A school board candidate with more than half the primary vote is elected outright; otherwise the top two go to April
quote: A candidate receiving more than fifty percent (50%) of the votes cast in the board of education primary election shall be elected to the office.

claim: With only two school board candidates, the race goes straight to April
quote: If only two candidates qualify to have their names appear on the ballot, the names of both candidates shall appear on the ballot at the board of education general election.

claim: Every registered voter living in the district may vote in a school election (no party ballot)
quote: To be eligible to vote in a school district election or a technology center school district election, a person must be registered with the county election board at an address located within the geographical boundaries of the district.

claim: School board candidates file where county candidates file
quote: shall file declarations of candidacy in the same place and with the same officials as candidates for county office

claim: An independent district with a five-member board elects members to five-year terms
quote: Districts having a five-member board 5 5

claim: A seven-member board (four-year terms) may shrink to five members
quote: Any seven-member board shall have the option of reducing its board to a five-member board

claim: Board members represent board districts, one member per district
quote: One member of the board of education shall be elected by the electors of the school district to represent each such board district.

claim: Districts under 1,800 students may elect all members at large
quote: may choose not to establish board districts and may nominate and elect all board members at large

claim: Districts over 10,000 students use a two-step election within each board district
quote: In a school district having more than ten thousand (10,000) children in average daily membership

claim: A district over 30,000 students may add an at-large board chair elected for four years
quote: may be expanded to add a member who shall be elected at large for a term of four (4) years and who shall serve as chair of the board

claim: The district attorney is nominated and elected in a district attorney's district, every four years, not by county
quote: there shall be nominated and elected in each and every district attorney's district in the State of Oklahoma, a district attorney

claim: "Township" in the constitution's county descriptions is a survey line
quote: Beginning on the township line between townships nineteen and twenty North

claim: In a council-manager city the council appoints the city manager
quote: The council shall appoint a city manager

claim: Elementary district boards have three members on three-year terms
quote: Elementary 3 3

claim: Seven-member independent district boards serve four-year terms
quote: member board unless an election is conducted pursuant to subsection C of this section 7 4
